title: CDL drug and alcohol testing practice questions
description: Free CDL drug and alcohol testing practice questions on 49 CFR Part 382. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.topic: Who is covered and key definitions
questions.question: How does the Part 382 definition of "driver" describe who is included?

options.A: Only full-time drivers on the employer's payroll
options.B: Any person who operates a CMV, including casual, intermittent or occasional drivers, leased drivers and independent owner-operator contractors
options.C: Only drivers who hold a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
options.D: Only drivers who drive more than 50 percent of their working time

questions.explanation: "Driver means any person who operates a commercial motor vehicle." It "includes, but is not limited to: Full time, regularly employed drivers; casual, intermittent or occasional drivers; leased drivers and independent owner-operator contractors."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.107, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Driver means any person who operates a commercial motor vehicle. This includes, but is not limited to: Full time, regularly employed drivers; casual, intermittent or occasional drivers; leased drivers and independent owner-operator contractors.

questions.topic: Who is covered and key definitions
questions.question: What random testing arrangement does 382.103(b) require of an employer who employs only himself or herself as a driver?

options.A: None; a sole driver is exempt from random testing
options.B: A self-test once each calendar year on a date the driver picks
options.C: Random testing only after a first violation
options.D: A random testing program of two or more covered employees in the random testing selection pool

questions.explanation: Such an employer "shall implement a random alcohol and controlled substances testing program of two or more covered employees in the random testing selection pool."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.103, Applicability (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An employer who employs only himself/herself as a driver shall implement a random alcohol and controlled substances testing program of two or more covered employees in the random testing selection pool.

questions.question: What alcohol concentration does 382.201 name as the level at which a driver must not report for duty or remain on duty requiring safety-sensitive functions?

options.A: 0.04 or greater
options.B: 0.08 or greater
options.C: 0.10 or greater
options.D: 0.06 or greater

questions.explanation: "No driver shall report for duty or remain on duty requiring the performance of safety-sensitive functions while having an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.201, Alcohol concentration (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No driver shall report for duty or remain on duty requiring the performance of safety-sensitive functions while having an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater.

questions.question: What period does the pre-duty use rule in 382.207 set between using alcohol and performing safety-sensitive functions?

options.A: Thirty minutes
options.B: One hour
options.C: Four hours
options.D: Two hours

questions.explanation: "No driver shall perform safety-sensitive functions within four hours after using alcohol."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.207, Pre-duty use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No driver shall perform safety-sensitive functions within four hours after using alcohol.

questions.question: Under 382.209, a driver who is required to take a post-accident alcohol test must not use alcohol for what period?

options.A: Two hours after the accident
options.B: Four hours after the accident, whether or not tested
options.C: Eight hours following the accident, or until he/she undergoes a post-accident alcohol test, whichever occurs first
options.D: One hour after the accident

questions.explanation: "No driver required to take a post-accident alcohol test under § 382.303 shall use alcohol for eight hours following the accident, or until he/she undergoes a post-accident alcohol test, whichever occurs first."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.209, Use following an accident (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No driver required to take a post-accident alcohol test under § 382.303 shall use alcohol for eight hours following the accident, or until he/she undergoes a post-accident alcohol test, whichever occurs first.

questions.question: A driver tested under subpart C has an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or greater but less than 0.04. Under 382.505(a), when may the driver next perform safety-sensitive functions for an employer?

options.A: At the start of the driver's next regularly scheduled duty period, but not less than 24 hours following administration of the test
options.B: Four hours after the test
options.C: Immediately, because the result is below 0.04
options.D: Eight hours after the test

questions.explanation: The driver may not perform safety-sensitive functions "until the start of the driver's next regularly scheduled duty period, but not less than 24 hours following administration of the test."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.505, Other alcohol-related conduct (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No driver tested under the provisions of subpart C of this part who is found to have an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or greater but less than 0.04 shall perform or continue to perform safety-sensitive functions for an employer, including driving a commercial motor vehicle, nor shall an employer permit the driver to perform or continue to perform safety-sensitive functions, until the start of the driver's next regularly scheduled duty period, but not less than 24 hours following administration of the test.

questions.question: Under 382.213(b), when may a driver use a non-Schedule I drug listed in the other schedules of 21 CFR part 1308 and still report for safety-sensitive duty?

options.A: When the driver takes it only on days off and feels fine at work
options.B: When the driver has told a coworker about it
options.C: When the driver has used it for 30 days without side effects
options.D: When the use is prescribed by a licensed medical practitioner who is familiar with the driver's medical history and has advised the driver it will not adversely affect safe CMV operation

questions.explanation: The ban applies "except when the use is prescribed by a licensed medical practitioner, as defined in § 382.107, who is familiar with the driver's medical history and has advised the driver that the substance will not adversely affect the driver's ability to safely operate a commercial motor vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.213, Controlled substance use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No driver shall report for duty or remain on duty requiring the performance of safety-sensitive functions when the driver uses any non-Schedule I drug or substance that is identified in the other Schedules in 21 CFR part 1308 except when the use is prescribed by a licensed medical practitioner, as defined in § 382.107, who is familiar with the driver's medical history and has advised the driver that the substance will not adversely affect the driver's ability to safely operate a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which of these is listed in the 382.107 definition of "refuse to submit" to a test?

options.A: Leaving the testing site before the testing process commences for a pre-employment test
options.B: Being reported by the MRO as having a verified adulterated or substituted test result
options.C: Asking the employer in writing for copies of past test records
options.D: Having a test result that the MRO cancels

questions.explanation: The definition includes a driver who "Is reported by the MRO as having a verified adulterated or substituted test result." By contrast, leaving before a pre-employment test process commences "is not deemed to have refused to test."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.107, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (9) Is reported by the MRO as having a verified adulterated or substituted test result.

questions.question: Unless the employer uses the exception in 382.301(b), what must an employer have received before letting a driver it intends to hire or use perform safety-sensitive functions?

options.A: A controlled substances test result from the MRO or C/TPA indicating a verified negative test result for that driver
options.B: A signed statement from the driver that he or she does not use drugs
options.C: A receipt from the collection site showing a specimen was given
options.D: A negative pre-employment alcohol test only

questions.explanation: "No employer shall allow a driver, who the employer intends to hire or use, to perform safety-sensitive functions unless the employer has received a controlled substances test result from the MRO or C/TPA indicating a verified negative test result for that driver."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.301, Pre-employment testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No employer shall allow a driver, who the employer intends to hire or use, to perform safety-sensitive functions unless the employer has received a controlled substances test result from the MRO or C/TPA indicating a verified negative test result for that driver.

questions.question: What does 382.301(d) say about pre-employment alcohol testing?

options.A: It is required for every new driver
options.B: It is prohibited under Part 382
options.C: An employer may, but is not required to, conduct it
options.D: It is required only for drivers with a prior violation

questions.explanation: "An employer may, but is not required to, conduct pre-employment alcohol testing under this part."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.301, Pre-employment testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An employer may, but is not required to, conduct pre-employment alcohol testing under this part.

questions.question: After an accident involving a CMV on a public road in commerce that involved the loss of human life, which surviving drivers must the employer test for alcohol under 382.303(a)(1)?

options.A: Only drivers who receive a citation within 8 hours
options.B: Each surviving driver who was performing safety-sensitive functions with respect to the vehicle
options.C: Only drivers a police report finds at fault
options.D: Only drivers whose vehicle had to be towed away

questions.explanation: The employer "shall test for alcohol for each of its surviving drivers: (1) Who was performing safety-sensitive functions with respect to the vehicle, if the accident involved the loss of human life". No citation is needed for this case.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.303, Post-accident testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: As soon as practicable following an occurrence involving a commercial motor vehicle operating on a public road in commerce, each employer shall test for alcohol for each of its surviving drivers: (1) Who was performing safety-sensitive functions with respect to the vehicle, if the accident involved the loss of human life; or

questions.question: For a non-fatal accident with disabling damage requiring a tow away, what citation window does 382.303(b)(2) set for the post-accident controlled substances test?

options.A: 8 hours
options.B: 24 hours
options.C: 72 hours
options.D: Thirty-two hours

questions.explanation: The test applies to a surviving driver "Who receives a citation within thirty-two hours of the occurrence under State or local law for a moving traffic violation arising from the accident".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.303, Post-accident testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 382.303(d)(1) require when a required post-accident alcohol test has not been administered within eight hours following the accident?

options.A: The employer shall cease attempts to administer an alcohol test and prepare and maintain a record of the reasons
options.B: The employer keeps trying until 32 hours have passed
options.C: The employer replaces it with a controlled substances test and keeps no record
options.D: The driver may sign a statement instead of testing

questions.explanation: "If a test required by this section is not administered within eight hours following the accident, the employer shall cease attempts to administer an alcohol test and shall prepare and maintain the same record."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.303, Post-accident testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If a test required by this section is not administered within eight hours following the accident, the employer shall cease attempts to administer an alcohol test and shall prepare and maintain the same record.

questions.question: How does 382.305(k) require the dates of random alcohol and controlled substances tests to be set?

options.A: Announced to drivers at least one week ahead
options.B: Grouped in the first quarter of each year
options.C: Unannounced and spread reasonably throughout the calendar year
options.D: On each driver's hiring anniversary

questions.explanation: Random tests must be "unannounced", and the dates must be "spread reasonably throughout the calendar year."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.305, Random testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each employer shall ensure that random alcohol and controlled substances tests conducted under this part are unannounced. (2) Each employer shall ensure that the dates for administering random alcohol and controlled substances tests conducted under this part are spread reasonably throughout the calendar year.

questions.question: When the FMCSA Administrator changes the minimum annual percentage rate for random alcohol testing, when does the new rate apply?

options.A: On the day it is published
options.B: 90 days after the employer receives a letter
options.C: When each employer chooses
options.D: Starting January 1 of the calendar year following publication in the Federal Register

questions.explanation: "The new minimum annual percentage rate for random alcohol testing will be applicable starting January 1 of the calendar year following publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.305, Random testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The new minimum annual percentage rate for random alcohol testing will be applicable starting January 1 of the calendar year following publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.

questions.question: Under 382.307(c), who must make the observations for reasonable suspicion testing?

options.A: Any coworker who saw the driver
options.B: A supervisor or company official who is trained in accordance with 382.603
options.C: The medical review officer
options.D: A law enforcement officer only

questions.explanation: "The required observations for alcohol and/or controlled substances reasonable suspicion testing shall be made by a supervisor or company official who is trained in accordance with § 382.603."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.307, Reasonable suspicion testing (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The required observations for alcohol and/or controlled substances reasonable suspicion testing shall be made by a supervisor or company official who is trained in accordance with § 382.603.

questions.question: What minimum training does 382.603 set for persons designated to supervise drivers?

options.A: At least 60 minutes on alcohol misuse and at least an additional 60 minutes on controlled substances use
options.B: 30 minutes in total on both subjects
options.C: 60 minutes in total covering both subjects together
options.D: 15 minutes on alcohol misuse only

questions.explanation: Supervisors must "receive at least 60 minutes of training on alcohol misuse and receive at least an additional 60 minutes of training on controlled substances use." "Recurrent training for supervisory personnel is not required."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.603, Training for supervisors (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each employer shall ensure that all persons designated to supervise drivers receive at least 60 minutes of training on alcohol misuse and receive at least an additional 60 minutes of training on controlled substances use.

questions.topic: Removal, return to duty and follow-up
questions.question: A CDL holder violated the prohibitions and has not completed part 40, subpart O. By when does 382.415 require written notice to all current employers?

options.A: Within 30 days of the violation
options.B: At the next annual Clearinghouse query
options.C: Only when the driver changes employers
options.D: Before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice of the violation, or prior to performing any safety-sensitive function, whichever comes first

questions.explanation: "The notification must be made before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice of the violation, or prior to performing any safety-sensitive function, whichever comes first."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.415, Notification to employers of a controlled substances or alcohol testing program violation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The notification must be made before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice of the violation, or prior to performing any safety-sensitive function, whichever comes first.

questions.question: Under 382.701(b)(3), what must an employer do when a limited query shows that information exists in the Clearinghouse about a driver?

options.A: Nothing until the next annual query
options.B: Send the driver for a new random test instead
options.C: Conduct a full query within 24 hours of conducting the limited query
options.D: Ask the driver to describe the information verbally

questions.explanation: "If the limited query shows that information exists in the Clearinghouse about the individual driver, the employer must conduct a full query, in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section, within 24 hours of conducting the limited query."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 382.701, Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the limited query shows that information exists in the Clearinghouse about the individual driver, the employer must conduct a full query, in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section, within 24 hours of conducting the limited query.

questions.question: What minimum retention period does 382.401(b) set for an employer's records of driver verified positive controlled substances test results?

options.A: One year
options.B: Five years
options.C: Two years
options.D: Three years

questions.explanation: Under "Five years. The following records shall be maintained for a minimum of five years", the list includes "Records of driver verified positive controlled substances test results".
